solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle badly functioning? Stop

definitions.note: an organ stop is a set of pipes or a voice the organist can select

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ill can mean badly, as in 'ill-treated'
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A car that is barely running finally gives up and stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb at the end of the motoring story, but it is the noun: an organ stop imitating bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Some organs have a stop of that name that imitates a set of tuned bells.

clue.text: Mention about great wrong coming from dangerous product

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the mention word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to cite is to mention

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes how badly wrong things can go with a dangerous product.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking causes cancer and heart disease, so the thing smoked is a dangerous product.

clue.text: Snubs two groups of soldiers

parts.note: the first group is RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
the second group is the Buffs, an old British infantry regiment

explanation.surface: Two army units cold-shoulder each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The two groups of soldiers are the Royal Engineers (RE) and the Buffs, a historic regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff someone is to reject or snub them abruptly.

clue.text: See cold drink offered by venue

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A cold beer is on offer at the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a place where something happens, the setting or scene, much as a venue is.

clue.text: Rotten conclusion is distressing

parts.note: food gone off is rotten
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A dreadful ending is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offending causes hurt, displeasure or upset, which is distressing.

clue.text: Design not right for wooden shoe

indicators.note: 'not' says the letter for right must be absent from the design word

parts.note: a pattern is a design

explanation.surface: A shoemaker abandons a design that is not quite right for a clog.
explanation.definitionFit: A patten was a shoe or overshoe raised on a wooden sole or iron ring to keep the feet out of mud.

clue.text: Endlessly urged to accept one gift

indicators.note: the shortened word accepts, taking in, the other piece
'Endlessly' says the final letter of the urged word is dropped

parts.note: pressed means urged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was pressed again and again to accept a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the D off PRESSED to leave PRESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is an informal British word for a present or gift.

clue.text: Travelled north and made a mistake

parts.note: to trip is to travel or make a journey
up means north, as on a map

explanation.surface: Someone headed north and went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tripped up is to blunder or be caught out, so it means erred.

clue.text: One Greek character or another in the course of drunken Noel

indicators.note: one piece sits within the course of, inside, the other
drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: another Greek character is psi, a letter of the same alphabet

explanation.surface: A tipsy man called Noel is a Greek character of one sort or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges the four letters of the name, and the second Greek letter goes inside after the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is one Greek character.

clue.text: Rock that's large rolling over

indicators.note: something rolling over turns upside down, so in this down-free across light the word is read backwards

parts.note: big means large

explanation.surface: A large boulder tumbles over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Rock' is the familiar nickname of Gibraltar, of which this is the short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar, a British territory on a great limestone promontory, is nicknamed the Rock and colloquially shortened to three letters.

clue.text: A rice feast organised in eateries

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A rice banquet is laid on in some restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-service restaurants are a type of eatery, so the plural matches the plural.

clue.text: Bird on heather twitching

parts.note: the ruff is a wading bird
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A bird perched on the heather is twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffling feathers or surfaces means disturbing them with small rippling movements, close to twitching.

clue.text: Contribute, not in a stiff manner

definitions.meaning: an adverb from supple: in a flexible, lithe way

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to provide; the other is the rarely seen adverb of supple, meaning flexibly.

clue.text: Donald having time by river

parts.note: the Usk is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: Someone called Donald spends some time beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald is not a duck or a president here but the Polish politician who was President of the European Council.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald is the first name of the Polish prime minister and former European Council president with this surname.

clue.text: Town in Kent with tiger on the loose

indicators.note: letters on the loose run free and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A tiger is loose in a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a misdirection: the town is in Northamptonshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in Northamptonshire, so 'Town' defines it by example.

clue.text: Expanding daughter is needing looking after

parts.note: tending means looking after

explanation.surface: A pregnant daughter needs someone to look after her.
explanation.definitionFit: Distending means swelling or expanding, as a stomach does.

clue.text: Like a sort of solid figure in test that the male doctor's probed

definitions.text: Like a sort of solid figure

indicators.note: the test word is probed, entered, by the other pieces

parts.note: a trial is a test
he is the male pronoun
DR is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: In an examination a male doctor probes a solid figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trihedral angle or solid is formed by three planes meeting at a point, describing a kind of solid figure.

clue.text: Get maiden that's awkward paired up

indicators.note: awkward letters are put clumsily into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is paired with a young woman in an awkward match.
explanation.definitionFit: Geminated means doubled or arranged in pairs, from the Latin for twin.

clue.text: Region in which eating alas is terrible

indicators.note: letters that are terrible are in a bad state, here jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A region where the food, alas, is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the region of eastern England covering Norfolk, Suffolk and parts of Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a named geographical region of England, so 'Region' works as a definition by example.

clue.text: Eternal message of some wrinkle-defying products?

definitions.meaning: read as two words: an anti-wrinkle cream's promise of less age

explanation.definitionFit: Timeless things never grow old; split, the letters make an advertising promise of looking younger.

clue.text: Certain exhibitionists, possibly mad, seen around underground area?

indicators.note: the mad word is seen around, enclosing, the other piece

parts.note: nuts means mad
Dis is the Roman underworld

explanation.surface: Some exhibitionists, perhaps crazy, are spotted near the underground.
explanation.definitionFit: People who go about without clothes expose themselves, so naturists are a kind of exhibitionist.

clue.text: Hairstyle of supermodel

indicators.note: 'of' signals letters taken out of the word that follows, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A supermodel's hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemically set wave or curl is a common hairstyle, short for permanent wave.

clue.text: Standard record introducing one large book

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A standard recording introduces a large volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example of a type, the standard by which others are judged.

clue.text: Bird — cat finally caught it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: 'finally' takes the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A cat eventually catches a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small British bird, a name for the blue tit or any tit.

clue.text: Suffer detention, as witnessed

definitions.meaning: read as two words: to be detained or kept in custody

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the letters say 'to be detained'; as one word they are the past tense of behold, meaning saw.

clue.text: County stocks old books I love

indicators.note: a shop that stocks goods holds them inside, so the county word holds the other pieces

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A shop in a county sells old books, which the speaker loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is deep loyal affection, a close synonym of love.

clue.text: Demon drink maybe that was once thought to cause illnesses?

definitions.text: drink maybe that was once thought to cause illnesses?
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: a harmful liquor, spirit as in strong drink, blamed for sickness in the past

explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent supernatural being is a demon; the second reading plays on spirit as alcohol and on old beliefs that malign beings caused disease.

clue.text: Love abstaining from booze? That's excessive!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: A lover who has given up drink is told that is going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters abbreviate 'over the top', meaning excessive or exaggerated.

clue.text: Five bad actions suppressing good getting digital gestures

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, so the bad actions word closes over the good letter

parts.note: sins are bad actions

explanation.surface: Five misdeeds that crush goodness lead to rude gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the two-finger gesture with the palm turned inwards is an insult; 'digital' means made with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two raised fingers forming a letter shape are gestures made with the digits, hence digital.

clue.text: See fish jerk crossing lake

indicators.note: the lake letter crosses into the middle of the jerk word

parts.note: a fathead is a stupid person, a jerk

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at a fish that has jerked across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here, telling the solver to look at the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of several bottom-dwelling fish with flattened heads, found especially off Australia.
